# graphhopper

**GraphHopper, the offline router behind the browser map's car, bike, foot and hiking routes**

- **Version recorded:** 11.1
- **Categories:** `navigation-maps`
- **Upstream:** <https://github.com/graphhopper/graphhopper>
- **Needs first:** `default-jre-headless`
- **Needs Java:** 17 or newer — read with `java -version` at plan time (a metapackage's version does not say which Java it brings); deferred from a profile on a machine below it, refused by name, nothing fetched to meet it

## What it does

Installs GraphHopper, an offline route planner, as one Java file under /usr/local/share/hammunition/graphhopper/. `hammunition reference serve` runs it on this machine only while the browser map is open, over the route graph `graphhopper-graph` builds from your map regions, and the map's Route control draws its car, bike, foot and hiking routes, with turn-by-turn directions. Its hiking profile reads how hard a trail is (`sac_scale`), and its foot profile keeps off mountain paths.

## Why you would want it

The browser map shows where things are; this lets it say how to get there, from your GPS position when the tether is running, with no network. It is the offline alternative to GraphHopper's own website and to a phone's map app. On the desktop, QMapShack's routers (Routino and BRouter) and CoMaps' own routing do the same job in their programs; this is the one for the browser page.

## Before it will work

Java (default-jre-headless, installed with it). The route graph from `graphhopper-graph`, which needs your map regions set in station config. Then `hammunition reference serve` and the map at http://127.0.0.1:8480/map/; the tether (`hammunition maps gps-tether`) for routes from where you are.

## Install and launch

- **Installed by name only** — it is in no profile.
- **Install:** `hammunition install graphhopper --dry-run`, read the plan, then run it without `--dry-run`.
- **Launch:** Its package ships its own commands and application-menu entry; a unit that ships none gets a generated terminal entry (**D-050**). `hammunition status` lists what is installed.
- **The install needs the network to:** the upstream files the plan lists, each checked against a pinned digest (or, for map and reference data, the publisher or a LAN mirror).

## Offline use

*Not yet documented for this application.* Read “Before it will work” above for what it needs; the install-time network line above is the only offline fact generated from the manifest. Internet, a local network and a radio link are three different things, and this page does not claim any of them works until it says so.

## How it installs

- prebuilt executable from https://repo1.maven.org/maven2/com/graphhopper/graphhopper-web/11.1/graphhopper-web-11.1.jar
  - Lands as /usr/local/share/hammunition/graphhopper/graphhopper-web-11.1.jar, mode 0644.

## What it changes on your machine

- **installed tree** — `/usr/local/share/hammunition/graphhopper` is created and handed to the operator who ran the install by an explicit `chown` step in the plan (**D-043**): the software keeps settings, logs or data beside its executable, so the tree has to be writable by whoever runs it. On a shared machine that means anyone who can act as that user can change what the launcher runs.
  - `/usr/local/share/hammunition` stays root-owned; the tree itself is replaced whole on every install, so anything the software wrote inside it is lost then
  - undo: `hammunition uninstall graphhopper` removes the tree

## Known problems

GraphHopper's own server answers every web page with `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` and checks no Host header (measured on 11.1). It listens on 127.0.0.1 only, on a port the system chooses each time `reference serve` starts, and the map reaches it through the reference server, which checks both; but while it runs, a web page from elsewhere in your browser that found that port could ask it for routes over your regions. Stop `reference serve` when you are not using the map. GraphHopper's own page at /maps/ on that port loads online base maps and is not used. Routes are flat: GraphHopper's elevation sources are downloaded online, and none reads the Copernicus tiles Hammunition installs. Not yet confirmed on hardware: a route drawn in a desktop browser on the field laptop; it was run on the development host over a synthetic region.

## Keeping it current

- probe: github release (`graphhopper/graphhopper`)
- strategy: reinstall
- A few releases a year. A new release is a new jar on Maven Central: download it once, check its sha256 against Central's .sha256 beside it, and bump the URL, the digest, the signature URL, the tree marker (the jar is named by version) and `version`. The route graph is rebuilt on the next install, because its record names the jar that built it, and a graph from another jar is never served.

The project's GitHub issues and its forum, https://discuss.graphhopper.com/; the profiles and custom models are documented in the repository's docs/ directory.
